hints: Think of this as redox, with dichromate being reduced to Cr3+ and hydrogen peroxide being oxidised to oxygen.
Write the two half-equations first: dichromate needs 6 electrons to make 2Cr3+, while each H2O2 gives 2 electrons to make O2.
Combine the halves so electrons cancel (you need 3 H2O2), then cancel any H+ that appears on both sides to finish balancing.
walkthrough:
**Spot the reduction and oxidation**

Lovely, let us start with what is happening. Cr in dichromate is +6 and goes to +3, so that is reduction. O in $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ is -1 and goes to 0 in $\text{O}_2$, so that is oxidation.

Reduction half-equation:
$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^+ + 6e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Write the oxidation half-equation**

Now the peroxide part. Each $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ loses 2 electrons to form $\text{O}_2$.

Oxidation half-equation:
$$\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}^+ + 2e^-$$

**Balance electrons and combine**

To cancel electrons, we need 6 electrons in total. So multiply the oxidation equation by 3.
$$3\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 3\text{O}_2 + 6\text{H}^+ + 6e^-$$
Add to the reduction equation and cancel $6e^-$ and $6\text{H}^+$ from both sides:
$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 8\text{H}^+ + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} + 3\text{O}_2$$

**Check atoms and charge**

Always do a quick check, it saves marks. Left: Cr 2, O 13, H 14, charge +6. Right: Cr 2, O 13, H 14, charge +6. Perfectly balanced.

options.A: Not balanced in atoms, charge or electrons. One H2O2 only supplies 2 electrons but dichromate needs 6 electrons, and 4O2 on the right gives far too many O atoms.
options.B: Correctly balanced. Atoms balance (Cr 2, H 14, O 13 on each side) and charge balances (+6 on each side). It comes from combining the 6-electron reduction with three 2-electron oxidations and cancelling H+.
options.C: Uses twice as much H2O2 as needed. Charge still looks like +6, but O atoms do not balance (19 on left, 22 on right). This is the trap of doubling the peroxide without rebalancing electrons and water.
options.D: Very close but H is not balanced. It forgets the final step of cancelling 6H+ from both sides after combining halves, leaving 14H+ on the left but only 14H on the right in water, plus charge is then +12 versus +6.
